stories.headline: President Rinkēvičs completes official visit to Azerbaijan, signs joint statement and documents
stories.summary: Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs conducted a three-day official visit to Azerbaijan (April 21–23), meeting President Ilham Aliyev in expanded-format talks, visiting the Alley of Martyrs, attending a bilateral business forum, and meeting the Milli Majlis speaker. A joint presidential statement and bilateral cooperation documents were signed; discussions covered trade, energy, transport, and the Azerbaijan-Armenia peace process.

stories.headline: Prime Minister Siliņa faces political backlash over €35,550 spent on airport VIP lounges
stories.summary: A disclosure that PM Evika Siliņa's office spent approximately €35,550 on airport VIP lounges over nearly three years (September 2023–April 2026) triggered sustained political and media criticism, with comparisons drawn to predecessor Kariņš's private-flight scandal. Siliņa defended the expenditure as routine security protocol; opposition parties escalated the controversy by invoking a prior KNAB inquiry into an Amsterdam lounge stay, while separate reporting showed opposition United List politicians also used VIP lounges.

stories.headline: Rinkēvičs and Baltic leaders condemn shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner
stories.summary: Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs publicly reacted via X on April 26 to an apparent assassination attempt on US President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, expressing shock and relief and stating 'violence has no place in politics.' His statement was widely quoted in Spanish- and Latvian-language international coverage of the incident.

stories.headline: Siliņa attends informal EU Council summit in Cyprus after bilateral meeting with Greek PM
stories.summary: PM Evika Siliņa visited Athens on April 23 for bilateral talks with Greek PM Kyriakos Mitsotakis, then participated in an informal European Council meeting in Cyprus (April 23–24) chaired by European Council President António Costa. At the summit she stressed EU support for Ukraine, called for measures to address the economic fallout from the Iran conflict including possible ETS payment deferrals, and welcomed the EU's approval of a €90bn loan to Ukraine.

stories.headline: Latvia approves EU-funded air defence procurement; Defence Minister discusses drone wall limits
stories.summary: On April 21, the Cabinet of Ministers approved use of the EU's SAFE instrument to finance procurement of drones, guided missiles, and related air defence systems including the domestically produced 'Blaze' interceptor drone. Defence Minister Andris Sprūds simultaneously gave interviews acknowledging that a defensive 'drone wall' along Latvia's borders can never provide absolute protection, and announced plans to acquire at least 500 additional interceptor drones in 2026.

stories.headline: State digital agency cancels election platform contracts with RIX Technologies, company threatens litigation
stories.summary: The State Digital Development Agency (VDAA) announced on April 21 that it had terminated contracts with RIX Technologies and four other companies providing election platform services, citing EPPO-flagged security and democratic-integrity risks. RIX Technologies rejected the contract termination terms and threatened court action; President Rinkēvičs had previously called for paper ballots for the upcoming Saeima elections citing the IT concerns. As of April 26 the dispute was escalating.

stories.headline: Saeima approves €30m airBaltic loan amid coalition tensions; Estonia declines stake
stories.summary: Following weeks of coalition friction—with junior partner ZZS demanding the transport minister's resignation as a condition of support—the Saeima approved a €30 million short-term loan to airBaltic. PM Siliņa had earlier warned of possible government collapse over the issue. Separately, an Estonian minister downplayed interest in taking a Baltic coordination stake in the airline, dampening Siliņa's pan-Baltic proposal from earlier in the month.

stories.headline: Sprūds featured in Euronews programme on Ukraine loan and US-NATO reliability
stories.summary: Defence Minister Andris Sprūds appeared on Euronews' flagship 'Europe Today' programme on April 23, the same day the EU formally unlocked its €90 billion Ukraine loan. Sprūds stated he has 'no doubt' that the US would come to the aid of NATO allies if needed, projecting confidence in the alliance despite tensions over US reliability under the Trump administration.

stories.headline: President Rinkēvičs speaks at 40th anniversary Chornobyl commemoration
stories.summary: President Edgars Rinkēvičs attended and addressed a Chornobyl disaster commemoration at Stradiņš Hospital on April 24–26, noting that the accident—which mobilised over 6,000 Latvians in clean-up operations—helped collapse the Soviet information empire. He called on the government and Saeima to address outstanding issues for Latvian Chornobyl liquidators.

stories.headline: Domestic violence law standoff: Siliņa denies ordering Istanbul Convention alternative; Welfare Ministry confirms no mandate received
stories.summary: The Welfare Ministry (led by ZZS) told a Saeima committee that it had received no instruction from PM Siliņa to draft a domestic violence prevention law intended as an alternative to the Istanbul Convention, which Latvia's parliament voted to denounce in 2023 but President Rinkēvičs declined to promulgate. A separate LSM article confirmed the Ministry planned to produce a draft by autumn 2026.

stories.headline: Swedbank branch manager sentenced to six years for defrauding elderly clients over 17 years
stories.summary: The Zemgale District Court sentenced a Swedbank employee, Larisa Bobrova, to six years in prison on April 22 for unlawfully managing client funds, document forgery, and payment instrument fraud between 2003 and 2020. She was ordered to repay the bank €202,555 and had exploited digitally inactive elderly clients across the Ogre and Bauska branches.
